question: If AI works better in some languages than others, who is left behind, and how do we include them?
reflection: Every language that AI learns to serve well opens knowledge and public services to more people.

sources.subject: 1,000s of AI agents crack brain data in 32 minutes
Claude Security, Hermes Robot Agent, Meta Byte Models

one_line: AI quality is uneven across languages and business results are uneven across companies, even as swarms of agents start to speed up real science.

top_stories.title: AI translation quality does not follow language size
top_stories.what: A Forward Future test of top models across seven languages found Swedish translated among the best and Hindi among the worst, with speaker numbers having almost no link to quality.
top_stories.why: Organisations serving Arabic speakers cannot assume global models are good enough and should test output quality in their own language and dialects.

top_stories.title: Thousands of agents scan brain-cell data in half an hour
top_stories.what: OpenAI, PerturbAI and Scripps Research ran thousands of AI agents over data from millions of mouse brain cells and, in 32 minutes, surfaced possible gene links to Alzheimer's and Parkinson's for lab follow-up.
top_stories.why: Large research datasets can be screened far faster, but the leads still need human checking and lab validation before anyone acts on them.

top_stories.title: Few companies see real returns from AI
top_stories.what: A Gartner survey of over 2,000 technology leaders reportedly found only 13% see meaningful returns from AI, while about half expect AI to raise their technology costs.
top_stories.why: The gap between spending and results is often about adoption, habits and process change, which is exactly where behavioural expertise adds value.

saudi_lens.text: Arabic and its dialects need their own quality testing; a Saudi benchmark for public-service language tasks would show where global models fall short.
As Saudi entities scale AI spending, measuring real returns, not just deployments, will matter for Vision 2030 programme reporting.

idea.title: Arabic service-language test
idea.pitch: Compare how leading AI models handle real Arabic citizen queries, in formal and Saudi dialect forms, scored by native-speaker reviewers.
idea.first_step: Collect 30 anonymised citizen questions in both formal Arabic and dialect and run them through three models.
